cards.text: Amos, one of the sheepherders of Tekoa, tells what he saw regarding Israel (Amos 1:1). He's just delivered the LORD's judgment on Israel for selling the needy for a pair of sandals (Amos 2:6). Now he says, "Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, O children of Israel," and the LORD has more to say.

cards.question: The LORD's word is against the whole family He brought up out of the land of ___.
Out of all the families of the earth, the LORD says He has known only Israel. So what does He say He will do because of that?

answers.text: Punish them for all their iniquities

cards.text: Hold on. "Only you have I known," and then "therefore I will punish you"? That's the boss telling you you're his favorite and, in the SAME breath, asking you to step into his office.
Then the questions start coming, one after another, like a drumbeat. "Can two walk together without agreeing where to go?"

cards.question: Next the questions turn to a lion in the forest. What do they point to about when a lion roars?

answers.text: He roars when he has prey
He roars when a storm comes
He roars to call his pride

cards.question: Then come a bird and a snare. The question about them points to bait having been set.
And the questions point to a trap springing from the ground only when it has something to ___.

cards.text: Now the picture leaves the forest and walks right into a city. A ram's horn sounds.

cards.question: When a ram's horn sounds in a city, the questions say the people ___.
The questions then turn to calamity coming to a city. They point to the LORD as the One who caused it.
Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing His plan first. Who does He reveal it to?

cards.text: Then comes the line this whole passage is named after. "The lion has roared—who will not fear?"

cards.question: In the second half of that line, the Lord GOD has spoken. The prophet says someone could keep quiet after hearing Him.

cards.text: Now a call goes out to the citadels of Ashdod, a Philistine city (Amos 1:8), and to the citadels of Egypt. They're told to assemble on the mountains of Samaria and take a good look.

cards.question: Ashdod and Egypt are invited to the mountains of Samaria. What are they told to see in the city?

answers.text: The great unrest and acts of oppression
The new walls going up around it
The great feast being held there

cards.question: The LORD says the people of that city know how to do right.

cards.text: A citadel is a fortress for keeping things safe, and if I had one, it'd be stacked to the ceiling with chocolate chips. So what does the LORD say is in theirs?

cards.question: The LORD says they store up ___ and ___ in their citadels.
Therefore the Lord GOD says what's coming for the land. What is it?

answers.text: A drought will dry it out

cards.text: That enemy will pull down their strongholds and plunder their citadels. All that violence stored up in there, and now somebody's coming to clean the place out.
Then the LORD gives a picture I bet Amos the sheepherder knew well: a shepherd snatching from the mouth of the lion two legs or a piece of an ear.

cards.question: Like that shepherd's rescue, the Israelites dwelling in Samaria will come out with almost nothing.

cards.text: Rescued, having just the corner of a bed or the cushion of a couch. That's calling the movers, and the only thing that makes it to the new place is ONE couch cushion.
Then the Lord GOD, the God of Hosts, calls out to hear and testify. Remember, friend, Jacob is the man God renamed Israel (Genesis 32:28).

cards.question: The Lord GOD, the God of Hosts, calls out to hear and testify. Who is the testimony against?

cards.text: Then the LORD talks about the day He punishes Israel for their transgressions. He'll visit destruction on the altars of Bethel, the town where Jeroboam, king of Israel, once set up a golden calf (1 Kings 12:29).

cards.question: What does the LORD say will happen to the horns of the altar at Bethel?

answers.text: They'll be cut off and fall to the ground
They'll be covered in fresh gold again
They'll be carried off to the land of Egypt

cards.question: Then come the houses. The LORD says He'll tear down the winter house but leave the summer house standing.

cards.text: Winter house, summer house, houses of ivory, great houses, the LORD says they all come down. These folks had a house for every season, and I had ONE junk drawer that I shared with a rubber band.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new. It repeats Amos 3:2, which card 3 already told and asked about, just to carry a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. Its joke also casts the LORD as a boss calling someone into his office, which edges toward humor aimed at God. Fold the reaction into a card that tells new verses, or cut it.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: Outside card 4's recap joke, stop 1 has almost no humor. Cards 1, 5, 9 and 13 read as plain narration with none of Papa Dorin's reactions, disbelief or self-deprecation. The run of rhetorical questions in 3:3-6 is a natural place for a real laugh that doesn't blur a fact.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The card spends its words defining a hard word: "A citadel is a fortress for keeping things safe." Citadel should get a dictionary pop-up instead.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: This story card brings up Jacob ("Jacob is the man God renamed Israel") right before card 12 asks who the testimony is against. The right answer is "The house of Jacob," so the card gives the answer away. "Remember, friend" also points back to a setup that never came earlier in this lesson. Card 11 also repeats card 12's setup ("calls out to hear and testify") almost word for word.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card says Jeroboam set up a golden calf at Bethel and cites only 1 Kings 12:29. That verse says "One he set up in Bethel, and the other in Dan." The golden calves are named in 1 Kings 12:28. The reference doesn't carry the fact it's attached to. It should be 1 Kings 12:28-29.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.
